fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not specify or test service conditions or oxidation performance at 1000–1150 °C, so it cannot establish suitability as a thermal-barrier-system bond coat.
The proposed 50% stand-off reduction, 20–30% thickness increase, and approximately 70 mm critical threshold are not supported by the cited evidence.
The intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated solution: optimized low-temperature ID-HVAF processing at the medium air/fuel setting produced an approximately 150 μm coating.
explanation: The alternative is scientifically plausible because the cited study supports the qualitative trends that shorter spray distance can reduce particle scattering, preserve impact energy, lower porosity, and reduce in-flight oxidation. The controlled two-condition experiment could test those deposition-stage claims. However, the evidence reports only a slight thickness trend and does not justify the proposed quantitative settings or gains. More importantly, the hypothesis omits the central service-performance requirement: formation and retention of a thin, continuous alumina TGO during high-temperature exposure. It provides no 1000–1150 °C oxidation schedule, mass-gain measurements, TGO characterization, interdiffusion assessment, or spallation criterion. It is therefore a plausible process alternative rather than a reconstruction of the optimized ID-HVAF intervention and its demonstrated oxidation behavior.
